results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 45 body units' summaries match their aligned spec paragraphs' controlling ideas in spec order; the three callout units match no spec paragraph.

Outliner marked review ¶2 (p08), Four Ways ¶3 (p14) and TCO ¶7 (p25) and a callout; each carries the single controlling idea its spec paragraph declares (the two pitches; the two mixed shapes; the comparison's generalizable lessons, with the run-rate as evidence for the first). The p25 difficulty is recorded under flow_is_followable.
Every unit ties to a supporting claim S1-S6 or serves the introduction/conclusion.

Tables are introduced or followed by a sentence saying what they show (shapes p13, capability table p17, nine lines p23a, cost table p25, stage table p34, trade-offs p33); quotations and figures are interpreted.

results.quote: **Where we are in the order's journey.** A jacket purchase depends on checkout, warehouse, payment, returns and finance systems.
results.finding: Declared elaboration carrying over 'comparing options on what they fix and cost'; the paragraph opens with a label and a new topic and does not pick up the comparison.

results.quote: This chapter's answer is to choose capability by capability, not by platform shape.
results.finding: Declared cause_effect carrying over Kestrel & Pine's choice of stay and surround and presenting the rule that choice applies; the opening sentence does not refer to that choice, so the answer reads as a restatement.

results.quote: Payment fees are the platform's largest revenue line at Shopify and Lightspeed
results.finding: Declared additional_support from fees linked to sales to fees linked to payments; no signal of the move from the first two lines to payment processing (flow reader B also stumbled here).

results.draft_locus: Lock-In and the Cost of Leaving ¶5
results.quote: The Lynchpin is lock-in by another name
results.finding: Declared example carrying over the exit questions and introducing what happens when they are never asked; the paragraph does not pick up the questions.

results.quote: "The chapter names these choices below" is vague. I could not tell what it pointed to.
results.finding: Closing sentence of the hook points nowhere identifiable.
results.corroborated_by: flowB §3 item 1 ('This is vague. Which choices, and where?')

results.quote: Staying was never introduced as an option in this section, so the sum does not match on first reading.
results.finding: 'Three options remain' includes staying on the platform, which was never introduced; the count does not add up.
results.corroborated_by: flowB §3 item 3 ('Staying had never been introduced as an option')

results.quote: "The platform's own till system for the stores (its POS) is evaluated in 2028" is out of place. Nothing before it prepares the reader for it.
results.finding: The POS deferral arrives unprepared in the decision paragraph.
results.corroborated_by: flowB §3 item 4 ('feels out of place in the decision paragraph')

results.draft_locus: Four Ways to Cover the Map ¶3
results.quote: "ERP" appears in the capability list and in the shapes table before "the ERP (enterprise resource planning: ...)" is expanded in the paragraph after the table.
results.finding: ERP is glossed after it has been used (it is already known to the audience; the late gloss jars).
results.corroborated_by: flowB §3 item 5 ('the ERP is defined in the mixed-shapes paragraph after the term has already appeared')

results.quote: It brings in a new figure ("72,000 returns") and a running sum that I had to work through twice.
results.finding: The €2.6M run-rate point, appended to 'Three things stand out', makes the reader reconstruct a sum from figures in an earlier paragraph.
results.corroborated_by: flowB §3 item 9 ('the densest passage in the chapter')

results.quote: The nested parentheses in "Zalando's Connected Retail technology (through which retailers sell their store stock on Zalando) will be discontinued ..." inside an outer parenthesis forced a re-read.
results.finding: Nested parentheses in the vendor-direction bullet.

results.quote: The opening gives the answer three times before the case starts ... Between them sits "Where we are in the order's journey.", which interrupts the move from the generic merchant to Kestrel & Pine.
results.finding: Answer repeated (key points, p03, p05) with the order's-journey note interrupting.

results.quote: "The first two lines depend on how the vendor prices. The pricing models themselves shape the cost line" says the same thing twice and slowed me down.
results.finding: Redundant opening pair of sentences.

results.quote: "Group stage with a team that owns joins, or a vendor", is unclear. I could not tell what "or a vendor" means.
results.finding: Ambiguous 'Fits when' cell for composable.

results.quote: The conditional recommendation ... sits under Trade-Offs, but it says it "follows from the five criteria". That made me look back to the previous section.
results.finding: Recommendation's placement under Trade-Offs sent the reader back to the criteria.

results.draft_locus: Lock-In and the Cost of Leaving ¶3
results.quote: "The rules point at SaaS platforms; the first cases will tell" sits awkwardly right after "an open legal question".
results.finding: Closing sentence seems to contradict the open-question sentence before it.

results.quote: "Two firms then pitch rebuilds, both citing the oversell." The agency's pitch is a headless storefront on the existing platform, which is not really a rebuild.

results.quote: Four Waypoint numbers arrive in one sentence, and W8 follows in the table. I had to stop and map them.
